data_quality_finding.detail: A subset of kallaama transcripts carries literal "?" where hook letters belong (e.g. "pu?ara" alongside correctly encoded "puɗara" elsewhere in the same corpus): pulaar 1,904/14,606 rows (13.0%), serer 252/12,486 (2.0%), wolof 0/7,140. Training or scoring on affected rows teaches/penalizes noise.
data_quality_finding.recommendation: Exclude affected rows from training mixes via an intra-word-"?" filter at mix-build time (same eligible-pool stage as the licence gate) until the source transcripts are repaired; the normalizer deliberately does NOT paper over the defect.

kinyarwanda.evidence: 0.04 combining marks per 1k chars (400-row sample of the 217k-row cv17 gb1 manifest)

pulaar.evidence: hook letters ɓ/ɗ/ƴ/ŋ are letters preserved by the base normalizer; not tone-marked

serer.evidence: Latin-extended letters present (ñ, é); ~5 combining marks per 1k chars are French loans, not tone

yemba.evidence: 150 combining marks per 1k chars; tone is phonemic (Grassfields); same policy as yoruba
